answer: In a market where AI agents buy comet images and prism calibration data, each seller must lock a refundable bond, and its share of paid jobs is proportional to its locked stake, not its account count. An attacker can forge a thousand identities, but splitting one bond among them gains no extra job share. Winning more influence requires tying up more capital; submitting data that fails an agreed, reproducible validation test forfeits the seller’s bond.
